proposals.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (about 6 eV), electronically insulating lithium-ion conductor. Its phosphate anion is resistant to oxidation near 4 V, so it should resist LiCoO2 at the cathode side. It is also chemically compatible with the sulfide Li6PS5Cl, since the P-O/Li chemistry is familiar from sulfide interface work. A thin Li3PO4 layer should block electron transfer and reduce interfacial decomposition.

Si-F bonds are very strong, which may limit the PF5/SCl-type products seen with the Ti and Zr fluorides. proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (about 6 eV), electronically insulating lithium-ion conductor. Its phosphate anion is resistant to oxidation near 4 V, so it should resist LiCoO2 at the cathode side. It is also chemically compatible with the sulfide Li6PS5Cl, since the P-O/Li chemistry is familiar from sulfide interface work. A thin Li3PO4 layer should block electron transfer and reduce interfacial decomposition.

LiF is a very wide-gap, highly ionic fluoride with strongly bonded F-, so it should be thermodynamically inert toward both LiCoO2 at 4 V and the sulfide Li6PS5Cl. The Li3PO4 result showed that oxyanion coatings can release P2O5, SO2 and SCl4 when they contact the sulfide, so a halide family is a chemically different choice that may avoid that reaction channel.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 was insulating with a wide gap but had a contact penalty of 0.337 eV/non-Li atom (bin 16) from decomposition against the sulfide, releasing P2O5, SO2 and SCl4. This suggests oxyanion chemistry is the problem, so I am exploring a halide.

proposal.hypothesis: Li4SiO4 is a wide-gap, Li-rich orthosilicate. Si4+ is already fully oxidized and hard to reduce, and the high Li2O content makes it basic, so it should not oxidize at 4 V against LiCoO2. The silicate is also a different chemistry from the phosphate and fluoride coatings tried so far. Its Si-O bonds may avoid the P2O5/SO2 release seen with Li3PO4, which could lower the sulfide contact penalty.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (bin 16) and LiF (bin 15) were both insulating with wide gaps but had sulfide contact penalties of about 0.31 to 0.34 eV/non-Li atom, so I am moving to a silicate family.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3BO3 is a wide-gap, Li-rich orthoborate. B3+ is fully oxidized and stable at 4 V against LiCoO2. Its B-O bonds are strong and unlike the P-O chemistry of Li3PO4, which released P2O5, SO2 and SCl4 against the sulfide. A borate may therefore react less with Li6PS5Cl and give a lower contact penalty. It is also a family not yet tested.
